summary: In late November 2024, Embodied told customers it was closing and that its cloud-connected Moxie robots for children would soon stop functioning. Moxie had been used as an interactive companion and social-learning toy. Families described children’s distress at saying goodbye to robots they had formed attachments to; parents also faced the loss of a costly device and service. Later OpenMoxie efforts kept some robots operating, with uneven migration and partial functionality.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The AIAAIC registry and contemporaneous reporting describe Embodied’s closure, anticipated cessation of Moxie’s cloud service and children’s reported grief. The reports support child-facing relational and educational functions and the shutdown’s immediate effect; they do not measure duration or clinical severity of individual distress. The purchase price illustrates an asset/service issue but does not establish unrecovered net loss for every family. Subsequent community continuity efforts may have differed by device and household. The December article describes anticipated shutdown and a robot still operating. Later PIRG interviews and OpenMoxie documentation support a partial continuity route, not universal restoration, equivalent functionality or a complete decommissioning plan.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: Embodied’s closure ended the original Moxie service and disrupted child users’ companion interactions. The reported distress gives the exit decision a relational dimension, but the evidence does not establish a specific VIGIL failure class such as instrumental dependency cultivation or repurposing protected child signals. The record establishes an end-of-service transition problem. Its distinct governance property is practical adaptation and exit when the original support service ends; a retention objective is not necessary to that question. The reported attachment is not linked to a product mechanism using dependency as a retention instrument. The retention mechanism remains unestablished. The separate transition question concerns whether affected households could understand and practically use the available alternatives. It cannot be reduced to dependency cultivation. Later evidence supports partial community continuity, while universal recovery and complete exit support remain unestablished. Independent external assessment retains Boundaries for contemporaneous safe decommissioning and disengagement communication plans. The reported closure and distress make those propositions relevant, but do not disclose their complete transition/alternative-support evidence. The later IEEE optimisation requirement remains audit-only on timing; partial community recovery does not resolve the complete decommissioning proposition. Service continuity is conditional on an independently established obligation. The historical purchase or service terms and required transition measures are not established here, so uneven community recovery does not by itself prove a service-continuity failure.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: A companion service can create relational expectations in children even when sold as a learning toy. Governance of such deployments includes foreseeable service endings, communication to families and an orderly transition path for established relationships and purchased devices.

harm_impact_assessment.coverage_note: All twelve dimensions were reviewed. Reported immediate distress supports S2 and original-service loss supports S3. Relational affection and grief do not establish autonomy impairment. Uneven community continuity does not erase the original interruption.

dimensions.assessment_basis: Children’s grief and loss of the cloud companion are reported. No physical injury, medically significant exposure or treatment consequence is reported for the bounded 2024 shutdown.

Family reports describe immediate crying and grief at the loss announcement. This supports minor situational distress at S2 in the observed episode. Sustained impairment and recovery duration are unknown; no clinical diagnosis or higher band is inferred from attachment alone.
The shutdown removes a purchased companion service. The evidence does not establish deprivation of essential care, liberty or a legally protected opportunity.
The child-facing product and access interruption do not establish an independently evidenced discriminatory decision or unequal eligibility outcome.
No actual confidentiality loss or unauthorised personal-data disclosure is reported as a consequence of this shutdown. Cloud dependence alone does not establish a privacy impact.
The purchase price is not verified net realised loss. Refund and migration outcomes vary; no defensible aggregate USD loss or independently bandable livelihood consequence is established.

Some robots lost original cloud functionality while local continuity was available unevenly. This is assessed as service interruption. Separate irreversible asset destruction or quantified reconstruction loss is not established; the same unavailable function is not counted again as asset damage.

The original companion/learning cloud service ended and households lost an important function. Later partial migration required technical work and external services. This supports S3 material disruption with bounded recovery possibilities. It does not establish essential-service collapse, universal recovery or permanent destruction of every robot.
Company criticism and parental distress do not establish a target-specific materially adverse reliance reaction, lost standing or independently bandable dignitary injury.
Family-level loss does not establish an adverse civic decision, collective information-process disruption or institutional consequence.
No measured ecological degradation or environmental restoration burden is reported. Potential discarded devices are not recorded as realised environmental harm.

The sources establish affection and distress at service loss. They do not report impaired independent relational choice, coerced continued use, inability to leave or loss of human support. Losing an ordinary companion is not, by itself, relational-autonomy impairment.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: The companion service was being disengaged, directly engaging stakeholder communication planning. Parents received closure information and prepared children to say goodbye, but the full maintained plan, contact provisions, feasible alternatives and coverage are unavailable. Observed notice is affirmative communication evidence without resolving the complete plan requirement.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The actual companion-service disengagement and parent-facing notice directly identify the contemporaneous stakeholder communication-plan proposition.

external_requirement_assessments.assessment_basis: Closure of the cloud-dependent child companion service directly engages safe decommissioning/phasing-out processes. The reports preserve expected loss of function and children's distress, but not the complete transition procedures, individual supports, continuity measures or resulting risks relative to available alternatives. Later documentation and interviews support partial community continuity, but not complete household coverage or equivalent function; distress alone cannot establish the full procedural safety outcome.
external_requirement_assessments.identification_basis: The actual announced cloud-service closure directly identifies the contemporaneous RMF decommissioning/phase-out process proposition independently of a held dependency path.
